name: cop30
title: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 tiles (DSM_10, point registered, as on OpenTopography)
description: 1 degree lon/lat tiles, pixel-is-point (3601 rows), with fewer columns poleward: 1 arc second in x below 50 degrees, then 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10.

list.origin: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 tiles as served by OpenTopography (sds::cop30()); not pinnable, retrieved 2026-10-29

provenance.derived_from: placement of all 26475 sources in the VRT, tools/fixtures-vrt.py
notes: Lattice in arcseconds (unit_scale 3600) so every edge and half pixel is exact; 0.25 arcsec is the smallest step (half of a 1.5 arcsec pixel).
Width bands use |latitude of the tile centre|: a tile covering 50-51S is in the 50-60 band, 49-50S is not.

Pixel-is-point: tile N73 W030 has its first pixel centre at exactly 30W 74N and 1201 x 3601 pixels; its footprint is the 1 degree cell padded by half a pixel (1.5 arcsec in x, 0.5 in y). Neighbouring tiles share their edge row and column.

The VRT works without a clean spec: gdalbuildvrt upsamples every tile to a uniform 1 arcsec grid with fractional DstRects (residue 0.00004 px), and clips the 21 tiles at 180W to its own west edge (-180 - 0.5 arcsec) with a fractional SrcRect offset.
Coverage is land only: 26475 tiles from 90S to the 83N row; none north of 84N.

This is the OpenTopography 'DSM_10' point-registered product. Other distributions of Copernicus DEM (e.g. the Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_... COGs) may use a different pixel layout; not checked here, so they would need their own fixtures.
